rationale: A whole MIND diet favored a sleep-quality score among women with diabetes and insomnia. Lentils were grouped with other legumes. The trial and Parkinson diet surveys leave boiled lentils and clinical insomnia severity open. The recovered guideline names lentils for fibre and weight management. A separate observational study links combined legumes and nuts intake to sleep quality, with a prepared lentil and clinical insomnia estimate still unresolved.

A Parkinson whole-saffron powder trial reported global cognition without a separate executive estimate. A dried-extract childhood ADHD trial gave inconclusive executive-related comparisons. SaiLuoTong improved a switching measure by a one-tailed test in older adults with mild cognitive impairment, but its interval spans zero and it combines three ingredients. Dried saffron and executive function in Parkinson disease remain unresolved. The 1994 oral ethanolic extract improved selected passive-avoidance outcomes after an ethanol challenge, with no clear effect in normal or scopolamine-challenged mice. These short-term memory tasks do not measure a dried-saffron specific clinical executive-function result. The verified imaging proceedings use saffron as a histology stain. The Parkinson powder study compared global cognition and patient-rated cognition, with the requested separate executive endpoint still unresolved.

Anxiety events differed among depression-treatment arms using rapeseed-oil placebo and different active drugs. GAD-7 was inconclusive for a formulation containing a hydrogenated rapeseed excipient. Animal and mixed-diet findings depend on oil processing and co-exposures. No cold-pressed Parkinson direction was established. The complete imaging proceedings identify canola oil as an artificial-phantom ingredient. They supply no ingested exposure or anxiety assessment.

A mixed evening meal including lentils had an inconclusive next-morning Epworth comparison in healthy adults. Both menus differed in several foods and energy. Canned-lentil effects on Parkinson daytime sleepiness remain unresolved. The guideline lists lentils for dietary management. Two additional adult datasets combine legumes with other foods or study whole dietary patterns. The Epworth association belongs to a whole-pattern analysis and gives no canned-lentil estimate.

Two other-oil or active-product comparisons in osteoarthritis supply no clear pain difference or oil-only estimate. A Mediterranean arthritis program reports less pain while changing many foods. The Sunola trial has an unresolved oil identity. Clinical Parkinson pain under cold-pressed canola remains unresolved. Verified chapter GA70 uses canola oil in an artificial phantom. The source does not supply a pain measure or a cold-pressed culinary exposure.
